overview.title: General Agreement On Tariffs And Trade
overview.definition: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was a legal agreement between many countries, whose overall purpose was to promote international trade by reducing or eliminating trade barriers such as tariffs or quotas. Operating from 1948 until 1995, it functioned as a provisional multilateral treaty rather than a formal international organization until it was replaced by the World Trade Organization (WTO).
overview.importanceInUpsc: GATT forms the foundational backbone of the global trading architecture in the Indian Economy syllabus (External Sector & International Organizations). UPSC frequently tests the evolution from GATT to WTO, India's historical stance during the Uruguay Round, and core principles like MFN and National Treatment.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin & Provisional Nature**: Established in **1947** (signed by 23 nations) and came into force on **January 1, 1948**. It was legally a provisional treaty because the proposed International Trade Organization (ITO) charter failed to get US ratification.
• **Core Principle 1 - Most-Favored-Nation (MFN)**: Article I of GATT mandates that any concession, favor, or immunity granted by a contracting party to any product originating in or destined for any other country must be granted **immediately and unconditionally** to the like product originating in or destined for the territories of all other contracting parties.
• **Core Principle 2 - National Treatment**: Article III mandates that imported goods must be treated no less favorably than domestically produced goods regarding internal taxes, regulations, and laws once they have cleared customs.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Through eight successive **Trade Rounds** (culminating in the Uruguay Round, 1986–1994), average tariffs on manufactured goods in industrial countries dropped from around 40% in 1947 to roughly 4% by the mid-1990s.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Headquarters & Secretariats**: Initially operated out of Geneva, Switzerland, which later became the permanent headquarters of the WTO.
• **Negotiation Sites**: Historic trade rounds took place across global hubs including Geneva (Switzerland), Annecy (France), Torquay (UK), Tokyo (Japan), and Punta del Este (Uruguay).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: GATT lacked a robust enforcement mechanism; countries could block dispute panel rulings (consensus rule). It largely ignored agriculture, textiles, services, and intellectual property in its early decades.
• **Policy Interventions**: The transition to the WTO eliminated the 'grandfather clause' and introduced an integrated, non-blockable dispute settlement mechanism.

items.title: Mnemonic for Core GATT Principles
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **M-N-T** (Most-Favored-Nation, National Treatment, Tariff reduction)
• **Decoded Meaning**: M = Treat all trading partners equally (MFN); N = Treat foreign goods like domestic goods (National Treatment); T = Tariffs are the preferred method of protection (no quotas).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly distinguishes core non-discrimination rules in statement-based MCQs.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: GATT = Goods only (until 1994); WTO = Goods + Services (GATS) + Intellectual Property (TRIPS).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements claiming 'GATT was a specialized agency of the United Nations.' This is INCORRECT. GATT was a standalone international trade treaty, whereas the WTO is an independent international organization.

Mains Value Addition: When writing about protectionism, global supply chains, or trade wars, use the historical evolution from GATT's tariff-cutting success to modern neo-protectionist challenges as a strong introductory analytical anchor.

keyTakeaways: GATT was established in 1948 as a provisional multilateral treaty and successfully drove down global industrial tariffs through eight major negotiating rounds.
The twin pillars of GATT non-discrimination were the Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) principle (Article I) and National Treatment (Article III).
GATT's structural weaknesses—such as weak dispute settlement and exclusion of services and agriculture—led to its replacement by the WTO via the 1994 Marrakesh Agreement.

question.en: Discuss the transition from GATT to the WTO. How did this shift impact the global trade architecture?
question.hi: Discuss the transition from GATT to the WTO. How did this shift impact the global trade architecture?

modelAnswer.en: The transition from GATT (1947) to WTO (1995) marked a shift from a provisional agreement to a permanent institutional framework. Key impacts include: 1. Inclusion of services (GATS) and intellectual property (TRIPS). 2. Stronger dispute settlement mechanism. 3. Broader scope covering non-tariff barriers. This created a more rule-based, predictable global trading system.
